subtitle: PCSX2
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own setup guide: "A Ratchet & Clank 2 US ISO (SCUS-97268)" and "PCSX2 Emulator". Its randomizer page adds "Only the PS2 versions of the game are supported" and states the PS3 Collection is not.
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: READ FROM THE WORLD'S OWN CODE: evilwb/APRac2 __init__.py line 74, `class Rac2World(World)` sets `game = "Ratchet & Clank 2"`. ⚠ TRAP: line 65 of the SAME file sets `game: str = "Ratchet & Clank 2 - Going Commando"` -- but that is on `class Rac2Web(WebWorld)`, the documentation page, not the World. The AP slot name is the World's. Taking the first match in the file writes the WebWorld's string and every Join then fails with an unknown game.
description: Ratchet & Clank 2: Going Commando as a multiworld. Gadgets, Platinum Bolts and Planet Coordinates are shuffled across the session. Requires the player's own US disc (SCUS-97268, version 1.01) and PCSX2 v1.7 or newer with PINE enabled on slot 28011.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PS2 title. The setup guide lists the disc among the player's own requirements: "A Ratchet & Clank 2 US ISO (SCUS-97268)". The world ships no game data and neither do we.

rom.description: Your own Ratchet & Clank 2: Going Commando disc image for PlayStation 2 -- the US release, version 1.01, disc serial SCUS-97268
rom._description_source: the world's own randomizer page, word for word: "Only the PS2 versions of the game are supported. US `version 1.01 (SCUS-97268)` is it for now." The setup guide repeats the serial.
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. Neither the setup guide nor the world's source states a checksum for the player's disc, so London can only warn, never reject -- and a hash is the one thing that must never be guessed.

emulator.name: PCSX2
emulator._source: the setup guide, word for word: "[PCSX2 Emulator]. Must be v1.7 or higher for the required PINE support." That is stated as a floor, so it is recorded as a minimum.

client.name: Ratchet & Clank 2 Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact name -- __init__.py line 25. Recorded so London can name it to the player; London never runs it.
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: evilwb/APRac2 __init__.py line 25, `Component("Ratchet & Clank 2 Client", func=run_client, component_type=Type.CLIENT, ...)`, and the transport lives in the world too -- pcsx2_interface/pine.py is a PINE client that talks to PCSX2 itself. So London must NOT read memory for this game. See docs/EXTERNAL_CLIENT_KIND.md.
client._protocol_source: extensions/pcsx2/extension.json declares {"protocol": "pine"} and PineBridge.Systems is ["PS2"]. The world speaks the same transport: pcsx2_interface/pine.py, and the setup guide has the player enable PINE in PCSX2 on slot 28011 -- the slot our bridge calls PINE_DEFAULT_SLOT. Both sides agree.
client._lua_note: No Lua. PINE is a TCP protocol spoken to PCSX2 directly; there is no connector script to load.

apworld._source: the world is published on its author's own releases page; the newest release read on 25 Aug 2026 is v0.6.4, carrying rac2.apworld and a sample YAML. Not bundled with Archipelago.
apworld._world_version_source: the newest release tag on evilwb/APRac2, read via the GitHub API 25 Aug 2026. ⚠ Not from archipelago.json: this world has none, so the tag is the only version it states.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the setup guide: "Installed Archipelago v0.5.0 or higher." Our client is 0.6.7, so this is satisfied.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: all 15 .py files at the top of the repository were searched. Container.py defines an `APProcedurePatch` and a patch_file_ending, but NO `APPatchExtension` appears anywhere -- so there are no custom Python patch steps for London's patcher to refuse.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block. This is a kind=world game: the world's own client produces and applies whatever it needs, and London never patches for it. Recording a patch block here would tell the launcher to try to patch the player's disc image.

world_by.name: evilwb
world_by._authors_source: the GitHub account that publishes the world (the repository owner). The world carries no archipelago.json and no credits list, so this may name a maintainer rather than every author.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: read from the repository: LICENSE.md begins "MIT License", and the GitHub API reports spdx_id MIT (25 Aug 2026).

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.

_removal_note: ⚠ Ratchet & Clank (the first game) and Ratchet & Clank 3: Up Your Arsenal were withdrawn at their author's request -- see catalog/removed.json. This is a DIFFERENT game by a DIFFERENT author (evilwb), and removed.json's own _matching rule says titles match WHOLE and "'Ratchet & Clank' must not block 'Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando'". The gate in build_plugins.check() was run and is green.
